name: Mandazi
summary: Light, cardamom-scented triangles of coconut milk dough, fried until puffed and golden.
story: Mandazi are a Swahili-coast fried bread eaten across Kenya and Tanzania at breakfast, with tea, or as a snack. They are sold in the morning at stalls and make a regular treat in many homes.

steps.title: Mix dry ingredients
steps.text: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, cardamom and salt in a large bowl until evenly combined.

steps.title: Add the wet
steps.text: Make a well, then pour in the coconut milk, beaten egg and melted butter. Stir with a spoon until a rough dough forms.

steps.title: Knead briefly
steps.text: Knead on a floured surface for 3-4 minutes until smooth and soft but not sticky. If sticky, add a spoon of flour; if dry, a splash of milk. Cover and rest for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Roll and cut
steps.text: Divide the dough in half and roll each piece into a circle about 6 mm thick. Cut into triangles or diamonds with a knife.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Heat the oil to 175 C (350 F). A small scrap of dough should bubble and float quickly within 5 seconds.

steps.title: Fry until golden
steps.text: Fry 4-5 pieces at a time for about 2 minutes per side. They should puff up and turn deep golden brown. Turn them gently with a slotted spoon.

steps.title: Drain and serve
steps.text: Drain on paper towels and let cool a few minutes. Serve warm with chai or coffee.

tips: If the oil is too hot, mandazi brown quickly and stay raw inside; too cool and they absorb oil.
Do not roll too thin or they will not puff properly.
Store in an airtight container and eat within 2 days; reheat briefly in the oven.
Add a teaspoon of grated lemon zest for a fresh note.

swaps.swap: Whole milk works but the flavour is less rich and tropical.
A pinch of cinnamon or nutmeg gives warmth, with a different aroma.
